changelog: Insert a single fallback ordering after C8 that, as a last resort, prefers cuts that keep numeral/quantifier+unit together first, then keeps finite verb/auxiliary adjacent to its immediately following core complement, and only then prefers punctuation/clause boundaries — to protect numeral–unit integrity (primary finding) while retaining punctuation as a tiebreak.
findings: The prompt treats cuts that separate a finite verb (or auxiliary) from its immediate core complement as acceptable, but doing so often creates an entailment/confusion (missing predicate, orphaned argument) when pieces are translated independently.
The prompt undervalues keeping numerals/quantifiers attached to their unit or measurement phrase; splitting them produces incoherent or contradicted short pieces.

diagnosis.why: Inserting the fallback changed tie-breaking so the model now prefers to keep numeral/quantifier+unit and finite-verb+immediate-complement adjacencies, which fixed a handful of short/numeric cases but—by demoting punctuation/clause boundaries—moved many cuts into prepositional/quote boundaries and other internal spots; bins show small gains for very short pieces (≤3, ≤7) but slight losses across mid and long bins (≤5, ≤10, ≤99), producing a near-zero net effect.
diagnosis.lesson: Don’t demote punctuation and clause boundaries so far in the tie-breaking order that modest numeral/unit/verb–complement protections cause many small regressions across medium and long spans.
